title: Quarterly Springboard: Hosted Endpoint Roadmap & Model Portfolio Horizon
creator: Maya Chen
description: Synthesize a quarterly roadmap artifact that maps endpoint capacity lanes (fast-path, hedged-reserve, overflow) to a prioritized model portfolio horizon (stable, experimental, sunset). Deliver a single decision-ready playbook for stakeholders (product, infra, reliability, sales) that prescribes: release windows, canary cadence, retirement triggers, capacity hedges, and cost/quality trade-offs. This ticket covers stakeholder interviews, scenario simulations for peak demand, recommended SLO guardrails, and a lightweight rollback/compatibility matrix for model variant substitution.
acceptance_criteria: A consolidated roadmap doc (PDF/Confluence) with lane-to-model mapping and release calendar for the quarter
Scenario simulation results showing latency and cost impact for 3 traffic shapes (baseline, 2x burst, regional outage)
Signed alignment from infra, reliability, and sales on capacity hedges and canary windows
A model retirement checklist with criteria and owner for each candidate model
An executable canary schedule that integrates with the Console rollout APIs and specifies fallback variants

decisions: Adopt three capacity lanes for the quarter: fast-path (low-latency), reserve (pre-warmed, moderate cost), overflow (best-effort, lowest cost)
Canary cadence: two short windows per release (2 x 1 hour) to balance feedback speed vs operational overhead
Retirement trigger: models with >10% regression on the canonical evaluation set for two consecutive weeks or <1% usage by endpoint over 90 days
Fallback policy: automated downgrade to quantized variant where quality loss is <2% and latency improvement >20%
risks: Region-specific capacity shortfalls during peak that require manual intervention; mitigation: pre-defined overflow routes and a runbook
Quality regressions from quantized fallbacks causing customer-visible errors; mitigation: stricter canary gates and per-customer opt-outs
Dependencies on Console automation (ENG-21456) may delay canary execution; mitigation: temporary manual scheduling process
Sales/customer pushback on model retirement decisions; mitigation: escalate to account leads and provide migration plans
